Section(s): 2.1. SMA model for sorption processes in IEC; 2.3.1. Introduction to the employed mechanistic model for chromatography

Text and equations in reading order:
    Based on these initial considerations, the time dependent change of the concentration of component $i$ on the adsorbent surface ($\partial q_{i}/\partial t$) in the SMA model is given by:
(1) \frac{\partial q_{i}}{\partial t}=k_{a d s,i}c_{i}\overline{{q_{1}}}^{\nu_{i}}-k_{d e s,i}c_{1}^{\nu_{i}}q_{i}\quad i>1    [code: PDE, computes q_{i}, code proposes balance]
(2) \Lambda=q_{1}+\sum_{i=2}^{n}\nu_{i}q_{i}    [code: algebraic, computes \Lambda, code proposes constitutive]
(3) \overline{q_{1}}=q_{1}-\sum_{i=2}^{n}\sigma_{i}q_{i}    [code: algebraic, computes \overline{q_1}, code proposes constitutive]
    with respect to $n$ components ($n=1$ [salt] + number of protein components). $\Lambda$, the parameter describing the ionic capacity of the adsorbent, limits the available binding places and displays the rivalry between salt ion concentration $q_1$ and the other bound components $q_i$ with their characteristic charges $\nu_i$ (cf. Eq. (2)). $\overline{q_i}$, the concentration of bound salt ions available for exchange with the protein, is given by the total salt ion concentration $q_1$ less the shielded ions determined by the protein specific steric factors ($\sigma_i$) in Eq. (3). If the assum...
    $ ( \partial q_i / \partial t = 0) $, the equation for the SMA-isotherm can be derived from the above equations to be:
(4) k_{i,e q}=\left(\frac{q_{i}}{c_{i}}\right)\left(\frac{c_{1}}{\Lambda-\sum_{i=2}^{n}(\nu_{i}+\sigma_{i})q_{i}}\right)^{\nu_{i}}\quad i>1    [code: algebraic, computes k_{i,eq}, code proposes constitutive]
    The results of SMA parameter determination following instructions in [14,16] (approach I) will be compared to the estimation of SMA parameters by fitting a mechanistic model for IEC chromatography processes to the monitored and time-resoluted concentrations of a protein component at column outlet.
    On column level, the time- and position-dependent change of concentration for the ith component, $ \partial c_i/\partial t $, is described by:
(7) \frac{\partial c_{i}}{\partial t}=-u_{i n t}\frac{\partial c_{i}}{\partial x}+D_{a x}\frac{\partial^{2}c_{i}}{\partial x^{2}}-\frac{1-\varepsilon_{c}}{\varepsilon_{c}}\cdot\frac{3}{r_{p}}k_{e f f,i}[c_{i}-c_{p,i}]    [code: PDE, computes c_{i}, code proposes balance]
    where the first term on the right hand side describes the convective transport through the column, the second term the dispersive transport and the third term the mass transfer to the particle surface, $ k_{eff,i} $ representing the lumped film diffusion coefficient and $ r_{p} $ the particle radius. $ u_{int} $ denotes the interstitial velocity, $ \varepsilon_{c} $ the column porosity, $ D_{ax} $ displays the axial dispersion, more precisely, a combined effect of dispersion and diffusive processes, dispersion being eddies and all effects implied by three dimensionality.
    Analogously, the time-dependent change of concentration on particle level for the ith component, $ \partial c_{p,i}/\partial t $, is described by:
(8) \frac{\partial c_{p,i}}{\partial t}=\frac{3}{\varepsilon_{p}r_{p}}k_{e f f,i}[c_{i}-c_{p,i}]-\frac{1-\varepsilon_{p}}{\varepsilon_{p}}\frac{\partial q_{i}}{\partial t}    [code: PDE, computes c_{p,i}, code proposes balance]
    with $ q_i $ denoting the concentration of particle-bound component i and $ \varepsilon_p $ the particle porosity. The second term of Eq. (8) describes ad- and desorption processes on particle level, i.e. the interaction between mobile and bound phase. Thus, the expression $ \partial q_i/\partial t $ is defined in Eq. (1) respectively, when a rapid equilibrium is assumed, in Eq. (4).

Symbols:
  q_{i}: Concentration of component i on the adsorbent surface (computed)
  k_{ads,i}: Adsorption rate constant for component i (parameter)
  c_{i}: Concentration of component i in the mobile phase on column level [M] (computed)
  \overline{q_1}: Available bound salt-ion concentration after steric shielding (computed)
  \nu_{i}: Characteristic charge of component i [-] (parameter)
  k_{des,i}: Desorption rate constant for component i (parameter)
  c_{1}: Mobile-phase concentration of salt component 1 [M] (variable)
  \Lambda: Ionic capacity of the adsorbent (computed)
  q_{1}: Salt-ion concentration (variable)
  \sigma_{i}: Steric factor of component i [-] (parameter)
  k_{i,eq}: Equilibrium coefficient of component i [-] (computed)
  u_{int}: Interstitial velocity [m s^-1] (variable)
  D_{ax}: Axial dispersion [m^2 s^-1] (parameter)
  \varepsilon_{c}: Column porosity [-] (parameter)
  r_{p}: Particle radius [m] (parameter)
  k_{eff,i}: Effective film transfer coefficient for component i [m/s] (parameter)
  c_{p,i}: Concentration of component i in the mobile phase on particle level [M] (computed)
  \varepsilon_{p}: Particle porosity [-] (parameter)

Model-wide assumptions (already recorded, do not repeat):
  - Rapid equilibrium is assumed.

Laws: 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8

laws.description: The bound concentration of component i changes through adsorption from the mobile phase and desorption back into it.
laws.quote: time dependent change of the concentration of component $i$ on the adsorbent surface in the SMA model is given by:
laws.law_type_reason: The accumulation rate of the bound component equals adsorption minus desorption.

laws.description: The adsorbent's ionic capacity is the salt-ion concentration plus the charge-weighted concentrations of bound components.
laws.quote: $\Lambda$, the parameter describing the ionic capacity of the adsorbent, limits the available binding places and displays the rivalry between salt ion concentration $q_1$ and the other bound components $q_i$ with their characteristic charges $\nu_i$
laws.law_type_reason: The equation defines the ionic capacity from the salt and bound-component concentrations.

laws.description: The exchange-available bound salt-ion concentration is the total bound salt concentration minus the amount shielded by bound proteins.
laws.quote: $\overline{q_i}$, the concentration of bound salt ions available for exchange with the protein, is given by the total salt ion concentration $q_1$ less the shielded ions determined by the protein specific steric factors ($\sigma_i$) in Eq. (3).
laws.law_type_reason: The equation defines the available salt-ion concentration from total salt and sterically shielded bound components.
laws.issue: The accompanying text labels the available salt-ion concentration as $\overline{q_i}$, but Eq. (3) and the symbol list define $\overline{q_1}$.

laws.description: The SMA equilibrium relation gives the component equilibrium coefficient from its bound-to-mobile concentration ratio and the salt-to-available-site ratio raised to the component charge.
laws.quote: the equation for the SMA-isotherm can be derived from the above equations to be:
laws.law_type_reason: This is an equilibrium isotherm relation that specifies the model's sorption behavior.

laws.description: The column-level mobile concentration changes through axial convection and dispersion, with mass transfer to the particles.
laws.quote: the first term on the right hand side describes the convective transport through the column, the second term the dispersive transport and the third term the mass transfer to the particle surface
laws.law_type_reason: The concentration accumulation is represented by transport within the column and exchange with the particle phase.

laws.description: The particle-level mobile concentration changes through exchange with the column fluid and adsorption or desorption involving the bound phase.
laws.quote: Analogously, the time-dependent change of concentration on particle level for the ith component, is described by: The second term of Eq. (8) describes ad- and desorption processes on particle level, i.e. the interaction between mobile and bound phase.
laws.law_type_reason: The particle-phase concentration accumulation equals transfer from the column fluid minus exchange with the bound phase.
